claim: Syzygy contains a private-LAN app-managed y-websocket relay with bounded native lifecycle and document recovery storage; bearer invitations still do not authenticate people and the update log is not an independent backup.
proved: The relay binds only explicit loopback/private IPs and runs without Node.js or PowerShell through the same Rust server code embedded in Syzygy.
Saved native configuration and child arguments contain routing and storage paths but no project room or invitation secret.
A graceful stdin-close signal exits and reaps the relay; the headless harness binds the same port afterward.
Two real y-websocket clients converge, every source client exits, the process restarts, and a new empty client recovers the document from server storage.
Only sync step/update frames are deduplicated and persisted; awareness is not restored after process restart.
Frame, room-client, room-byte, and room-record bounds are explicit; one partial crash tail is repaired while damaged headers and non-document records fail closed.
The exact product invitation and WebsocketProjectProvider/IndexedDB integration test passes against the native relay.
notProved: Authenticated participant identity, authorization roles, invitation revocation, or protection after a bearer invitation leaks.
Public TLS/WSS operation, log compaction/export, independent backup/restore, at-rest encryption, multi-room stress, or broader abuse controls.
Hostile binary-frame fuzzing, five-client rapid-edit soak, physical packaged two-install operation, cross-platform packet capture, or updater artifact inclusion.
